_comment: GOLDEN CORPUS for the ZTHREAT wire format — the shared truth for two
implementations that are written by hand in different languages:
producer  jetson/zvision/threat_protocol.py   (Python, on the edge box)
consumer  app/.../core/vision/ThreatProtocol.kt (Kotlin, on the tablets)
Both test suites read THIS FILE. Neither implementation is authoritative;
if you change one, this file and the other suite must agree or CI goes red.
Every vector below was MEASURED by running both implementations over the
same inputs, not hand-written. Before this corpus existed the two had
silently drifted in ten ways — see SYNC.md 2026-08-10 for the list.
parse_vectors:  frame -> contacts, or expect=null when the line is not a
ZTHREAT frame at all. A malformed contact is skipped, not
fatal, so expect=[] means 'a valid frame, all clear'.
format_vectors: contacts -> the exact bytes. Non-finite az/size arrive as
the JSON strings NaN / Infinity / -Infinity, since JSON
cannot carry them as numbers.
known_precision_limits: NOT assertions. The producer holds 64-bit floats
and the tablet 32-bit, so a value whose two roundings
straddle a decimal boundary is spelled differently by each
side. Both parsers accept either spelling and the values
differ by well under one wire digit. Recorded so nobody
'fixes' it, and so these inputs stay out of format_vectors.
